title: Yira, yira
author: Enrique Santos Discépolo
context: Argentina after the 1930 coup and the first blows of the Great Depression. Factories close and soup lines appear in Buenos Aires. Discépolo writes a song about a man abandoned by everyone, including luck.
stanzas: Y si un día la suerte,
se te escapa de la mano.

title: Mi noche triste
author: Pascual Contursi
context: Buenos Aires in 1917 is a city of immigrants crowded into conventillos. Contursi sets words to an existing tango melody, and Carlos Gardel sings it. It is often called the first tango-canción: the moment tango begins to tell stories.
stanzas: y en el cuarto quedó solo

title: Mano a mano
author: Celedonio Flores
context: The early 1920s: the arrabal watches its young women leave for the cabarets of the center. Celedonio Flores, a poet of the Boedo neighborhood, writes a farewell without reproach. Gardel records it the same year.
stanzas: y ahora que el mundo te mira
o la suerte te da vuelta,
